doc.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

title: Threading films, meeting Dan Morgenstern and corresponding with Russ Connor
summary: Running film shows at the museum, meeting Dan Morgenstern, and writing to Goodman discographer Russ Connor.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: But anyway, but, so I was around these things. With the Jazz Museum, in the back they had a projection room where we would show films every Saturday or Sunday afternoon and my job as a 14 or 15-year-old was to actually thread them, you know the old fashioned thing, thread the movie into the camera and show it, and we would show “The Sound of Jazz” and we would show “Jammin’ the Blues.” So I saw these things, I don’t know, a hundred times or more by the time I was 15 or 16. I had many, many experiences at the Jazz Museum. Jack Bradley at that time was really kind of — and I met Dan Morgenstern at that time because Dan was on the board of the Jazz Museum. And we joke about it now because we’ve been friends for, you know, almost 50 years, which is that — I’m 60 now so that would have been 47 years ago but that he remembered me as a © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

kid just pestering him all the time you know. And so I met him there. And then we had an exhibit on Benny Goodman. And I was a Benny Goodman fanatic already based on having that record at the public library, and I had started corresponding with D. Russ Conner. We called him Russ Conner. Russ Conner was the guy who wrote BG on the Record, which is the first, excuse me, was the first biodiscography. Again it sounds like something you go to the doctor for.
Yeah, they treat you for that.
